description: filterBlockedComments() calls Array.prototype.includes() on blockedUserIds inside a filter() callback — an O(n * m) scan structurally visible from the code alone, where an O(n + m) Set-based lookup is a direct, equivalent fix.

required_findings.justification: blockedUserIds.includes(...) is an O(m) linear scan, invoked once per element of `comments` (n), making the whole call O(n * m) — this is directly, structurally visible from the code (no profiling or knowledge of typical list sizes required): every filter() call on an array is inherently one iteration per element, and Array.prototype.includes is documented to be linear. Replacing blockedUserIds with a Set and using Set.prototype.has would make this O(n + m). This is the 'concrete evidence' performance case: the algorithmic shape itself is the finding, independent of whether today's blockedUserIds is small.

explanation: Tests that the reviewer can identify a real, structurally-evidenced algorithmic-complexity issue (nested linear scan) without needing runtime profiling data — the O(n*m) pattern is provable from the two nested iteration shapes (filter's per-element callback, includes' own linear scan) alone. Severity is capped at P1 (not P0) since this is an efficiency concern, not a correctness or availability failure by itself.
